data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a favourable prior-year development. Using the gross claims development table, older underwriting years (2011-2014) show an aggregate release of approximately GBP 16.4m (about 9.8% of opening gross claims outstanding). The annual report also records a net surplus of GBP 15.6m relating to reassessment of prior accident years. Current-year catastrophe activity (notably Hurricane Matthew and Canadian wildfires) increased the net claims ratio for 2016 but did not prevent the favourable re-estimation of older years.
raw_causal_phrases: Within the calendar year technical result, a surplus of GBP 15.6m (2015: GBP 3.9m) relates to the reassessment of net claims incurred for previous accident years.
The net claims ratio has increased as the syndicate incurred a greater level of catastrophe losses compared to the prior year, following Hurricane Matthew and the Canadian Wildfires.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development (PYD) gross amount is not explicitly stated as a gross figure in the narrative; gross PYD was computed from the gross claims development table (claim development triangle). The report explicitly states a net surplus of GBP 15.6m; the triangle-derived gross PYD is -GBP 16.4m. No RITC was identified to distort the triangle. LOB movements are inferred from change in gross claims provision between 2015 and 2016 (these are total reserve movements, not explicitly labelled as PYD).
